cases.name: Left bundle branch block (LBBB)

rationale.I: leadOverride.I replaces the QRS with two fused positive Gaussians (a 0.9 at mu 40, a 0.85 at mu 74) scaled by ws 1.667, giving a broad notched monophasic R with no septal q, plus st -0.08 and t -0.22 (discordant inverted T)

rationale.III: projection gives netR = 1.35*cos(20-120) = -0.23, so the else-branch renders r 0.108 / S -0.34 (rS), and the global ws 1.667 spreads that rS from roughly 12 to 97 ms, a clearly broad complex despite modest amplitude

rationale.V2: leadOverride.V2 is the same template but deeper (a -1.7) with st +0.22 and t +0.30, so broad QS with discordant ST elevation and tall upright T
rationale.V3: leadOverride.V3 gives a -1.3 broad QS with st +0.15 and t +0.25, i.e. persistent deep negativity plus discordant ST elevation where R-wave progression should have begun
rationale.V4: the only precordial lead with no leadOverride and no precordial override, so it uses normalPrecordial V4 (r 1.20, s -0.55, t 0.50, st 0) and is normal in shape, but the global qrsScale of 1.667 places r at 37 ms and s at 67 ms with sigma 12.5/15, rendering a ~150 ms wide complex
rationale.V5: leadOverride.V5 replaces the template with two positive humps (1.2 at mu 40, 1.15 at mu 74, x1.667) giving a broad notched M-shaped R that also erases the normal septal q, with st -0.12 and t -0.30
rationale.V6: leadOverride.V6 gives the same broad notched positive qrsComps with loss of the normalPrecordial septal q (-0.06), plus st -0.12 and t -0.28 discordant inversion

rationale.aVF: Global deltaWPW positive delta on netR 1.169 plus global qrsWidth 118 widens the complex 48 to 120 ms.
rationale.V1: normalPrecordial rS (r 0.20 < |s| 1.05) flips deltaA to -0.297 mV, producing a pseudo-Q/QS pattern with widening 52 to 130 ms from global qrsWidth.

rationale.V3: Template r 0.75 < |s| 1.05 flips deltaA negative, slurring the onset and widening the complex 56 to 130 ms.
rationale.V4: Template r 1.20 > |s| 0.55 gives deltaA=+0.297 mV, the classic slurred upstroke, with global qrsWidth widening it 54 to 128 ms.
rationale.V5: Template R-dominant (1.35 vs 0.28) gives a positive global delta slurring the upstroke, QRS 50 to 124 ms.
rationale.V6: Template R-dominant (1.05 vs 0.14) gives deltaA=+0.297 mV and global qrsWidth widens the complex 46 to 118 ms.

rationale.III: projection onto 120 deg gives -0.051 mV (0.38 mm depression at J), far below any reciprocal-change threshold a reader could call.

rationale.II: no leadOverride and stMag 0, so projection at 60 deg gives R 10.9 mm (smaller than the 13.5 mm normal baseline) with an unchanged upright T

cases.name: Right ventricular hypertrophy (RVH)

rationale.I: project(0,115,1.3) = -0.549 mV trips the negative branch of computeLead, rendering r 0.10 / S -0.65 - a net-negative lead I is never normal
rationale.II: pMag 0.2 projected at cos(15 deg) renders P at only 0.193 mV (1.9 mm), under the 2.5 mm P pulmonale threshold, and the P sigma stays 19 ms so it is not actually peaked; QRS/T otherwise normal
rationale.III: lead angle 120 is nearly parallel to axis 115 so R maxes at 1.295 mV (13 mm), still within normal limits for III, and its T (0.061) is numerically identical to the NSR case

rationale.V6: spec.precordial.V6 replaces r 1.05 / s -0.14 with r 0.35 / s -0.8, leaving a persistent deep S and R/S 0.44 in V6

cases.name: Hyperkalemia
cases.globalAbnormality: Global peaked/tented T waves plus flattened P waves in all 12 leads: flags.peakedT forces every lead's T to >=0.75 mV with tSig narrowed 54->26 (FWHM 127->61 ms) and flags.lowP scales every P to 25%, on a sinus rhythm with PR 210 ms and qrsWidth 118 ms (both global). No leadOverride, no precordial edits, stMag 0 - so there is no focal component at all.

rationale.I: Global peakedT floor raises T from 0.268 to 0.750 mV with tSig 26, and lowP cuts P to 0.017 mV, so this lead shows a tall narrow tented T over a nearly absent P.
rationale.II: peakedT gives a 0.750 mV narrow T (T/R 0.55 vs normal 0.24) and lowP drops P to 0.030 mV (0.3 mm), the textbook tented-T plus flat-P pair.
rationale.III: peakedT's 0.75 mV floor overrides the tiny projected T (0.061 mV normally), rendering a grossly disproportionate 7.5 mm narrow peaked T in a lead whose T is normally near-isoelectric.
rationale.aVR: Projection at -150 deg gives T = -0.345 normally, but peakedT preserves sign and floors magnitude at 0.75, so aVR renders a deep narrow symmetric inverted T (2.2x deeper, half the width) with P flattened to -0.027 mV - a direct global-flag effect, not a subtle ST reciprocal (stMag = 0).
rationale.aVL: netR projects to exactly 0 at axis 60 so the QRS is nearly flat, and peakedT lifts T from 0.120 to 0.750 mV - sampling shows the lead's peak deflection jumping 0.148 -> 0.779 mV, a giant T dwarfing the QRS.
rationale.aVF: peakedT raises T from 0.225 to 0.750 mV with tSig 26 and lowP flattens P to 0.025 mV, giving the same tented-T/flat-P morphology as II.
rationale.V1: The precordial template's t = -0.03 keeps a negative sign through Math.sign, so peakedT's 0.75 floor renders a deep 7.5 mm narrow inverted T where normally the T is flat - abnormal as drawn (an engine sign-preservation artifact, but a reader would call it).
rationale.V2: peakedT lifts the template T from 0.42 to the 0.750 mV floor with tSig 26, producing a narrow tented T, and lowP leaves P at 0.015 mV.
rationale.V3: peakedT's 1.6x multiplier takes T from 0.52 to 0.832 mV at tSig 26 - the tallest, narrowest T on the tracing and a keyLead for the tenting.
rationale.V4: peakedT scales T 0.50 -> 0.800 mV at tSig 26, a narrow 8 mm tented T with P flattened to 0.013 mV.
rationale.V5: peakedT floors T at 0.750 mV (from 0.42) with FWHM 61 ms, clearly out of proportion for a lateral precordial lead.
rationale.V6: peakedT more than doubles T from 0.36 to 0.750 mV at tSig 26, so even the lead with the smallest normal T shows a 7.5 mm narrow tented T over a 0.010 mV P.

cases.name: Hypokalemia
cases.globalAbnormality: Global repolarization abnormality: flattened T waves with prominent U waves in all 12 leads (flags flatT + uWave applied to every lead inside computeLead). Rhythm, rate (76), PR (160) and QRS width (90) are all normal, so the ST depressions in II/V4/V5 are focal add-ons, not the global finding.

rationale.I: global flatT cuts projected T to 0.094 mV (1.1 mm) while global uWave adds a 1.2 mm U, so the U exceeds the T
rationale.II: global flatT/uWave give a 1.2 mm T with a taller 1.3 mm U, plus leadOverride st -0.05 renders 0.5 mm of ST depression
rationale.III: global uWave adds a 1.3 mm U against a flatT-reduced 0.021 mV T, a 5.6x U/T ratio so the T-U complex reads as one broad hump
rationale.aVR: flatT leaves the projected T negative at -1.37 mm (normal direction for aVR) and the only finding is the +1.1 mm U that uWave sets as an unprojected positive constant, so its polarity is artifactual and it is the one lead where U does not exceed T
rationale.aVL: flatT drops the projected T to 0.42 mV-equivalent 0.4 mm while uWave adds a 1.2 mm U, giving a U nearly 3x the T
rationale.aVF: flatT reduces the projected T to 0.8 mm and global uWave adds a taller 1.2 mm U, so the U dominates the T
rationale.V1: global uWave sets the precordial U to 0.18 mV, rendering a frankly prominent 2.0 mm U against a flatT-nulled T of -0.01 mV
rationale.V2: flatT cuts the precordial template T from 4.2 mm to 1.4 mm and uWave adds a taller 1.6 mm U
rationale.V3: flatT reduces the template T from 5.2 mm to 2.0 mm and the 0.18 mV precordial U renders equally tall at 2.0 mm
rationale.V4: flatT halves the template T to 1.9 mm, uWave adds a 2.0 mm U, and leadOverride st -0.08 renders 0.7 mm of ST depression
